_comment: The guided-install contract of the PIM Manager. ONE-LINE-INSTALL (owner 2026-11-02): one line, the install cmdlet with every value as its own parameter, real values -- no answers file, no key, no licence in the command. Each answer below is a parameter of tools/setup/Install-PimManager.ps1 (and of the launcher Start-PimManagerInstall.ps1), validated by Test-PimInstallConfig. 'maps' = what the answer drives. Kept in step with Install-PimManager by tests/Test-PimGuidedInstall.ps1.
launcher: Start-PimManagerInstall.ps1, a file of the public GitHub release (https://github.com/KnudsenMorten/PIM4EntraPS/releases/latest/download/Start-PimManagerInstall.ps1): the same parameters; it checks itself and the release zip against the release, downloads the release and runs Install-PimManager from it. Two lines: Invoke-WebRequest https://github.com/KnudsenMorten/PIM4EntraPS/releases/latest/download/Start-PimManagerInstall.ps1 -OutFile Start-PimManagerInstall.ps1, then .\Start-PimManagerInstall.ps1 -TenantId <tenant id> -SubscriptionId <subscription id>. Pro / trial: the same run line, line 1 from the installer block's proUrl (the file itself decides the edition; no -Edition).

installer.urlFrom: Community: latestUrl (the public GitHub release copy, which installs Community). Pro and trial: proUrl (the copy Invardia hosts, which installs Pro). The two copies differ in ONE line; the run line is the same and never carries -Edition.
installer.parametersFrom: INSTALL-LINE-MINIMAL (owner 2026-11-03, all products): the run line carries ONLY the answers marked alwaysInLine (-TenantId, -SubscriptionId, -Location = the region) and the answers whose value differs from their 'default', each with the environment's value; a true bool = the switch alone. Left out: an empty value or list, a false bool, an answer at its default, an answer whose 'usedWhen' answer is not given / false (the option was not chosen: e.g. no network value without -PrivateNetwork, no -SupportAccess without -SupportAppId, no -PeerToHub without -HubVnetId), and an answer marked neverInLine. The installer prints its own -Resume line by the same rule (Get-PimInstallLineArgs).

commandLine: Every answer below is a PARAMETER of Install-PimManager (tenantId -> -TenantId, location -> -Location, superAdmins -> -SuperAdmins, ...; a bool is a switch). -TenantId and -SubscriptionId are required, every other answer takes its default, and installId is derived from tenant, subscription and resource group (pim-<12 hex>), so the same answers give the same names and the same state folder. -Resume = the same parameters again; the installation keeps its own state.
community: The GitHub release copy of the launcher (and Install-PimManager run with no edition) = edition 'community' (PIM Manager Community, free): one line says so; the licence step is skipped; the Core features (scenario S2), the Community updater (InvardiaCommunity, ring 3) and no msp.* feature gate. A licence can be added later in PIM Manager > Settings > Licence.
proLicence: Trial / Pro (the launcher copy from the installer block's proUrl; Install-PimManager -Edition Pro): one and the same install with the Pro updater (Invardia, -UpdateRing), deployed WITHOUT a licence. The licence step is a warning naming PIM Manager > Settings > Licence, and so is the end-of-install summary; the administrator adds the licence there, the Pro features switch on, and PIM Manager claims its install key itself (the claim is queued when the licence is stored).

exitCodes.1: a step failed -- fix it and -Resume

parameters.help: The Microsoft Entra tenant PIM manages. A licence added later is bound to it.
The Azure subscription that hosts PIM (Container Apps, Azure SQL).
Any Azure region; the installer checks before anything is created that every service PIM Manager needs is available there and suggests the nearest region that has them.
Created when it does not exist; an existing one is reused.

Off = the public install: the PIM Manager is reachable on the internet behind Microsoft Entra sign-in. On = the private network install: no public address (the Container Apps environment is internal); the database and the registry with public access DISABLED, reached only over private endpoints, no firewall rule; the registry's images built on its agent pool inside the network; the network hand-off at the end says what your network team peers and links. On an existing PUBLIC installation the same command converts it (data kept). The old -Exposure internal means the same (one release).
parameters.maps: Exposure internal + SqlPublicAccessDisabled + AcrPublicAccess false + AcrAgentPoolName pimpool (public install found: Convert-PimToPrivate first)

parameters.help: Private only. An existing virtual network to use instead of making one -- in the installation's subscription (any resource group), in the chosen region. Another subscription is refused.
The range of the virtual network the installation makes (not with -VnetId).
The name of the virtual network the installation makes (not with -VnetId).
The Container Apps subnet's name.
The Container Apps subnet: a /23 or larger, inside the VNet range. The old -SubnetAddressPrefix means the same (one release).
Private only. The subnet for the private endpoints.
Private only. A /28 or larger, not overlapping the apps subnet. Default: the /26 right after the apps subnet.
Private only. The resource group id of your central privatelink zones: used, never created or written. Empty = the installation makes its own zone in its resource group.
Private only. Your hub network: its range is checked for overlap; the peering and the zone link are made only when asked below, else they are on the network hand-off.
Private only, with -HubVnetId: peer the PIM network with the hub (both sides). Your rights on both networks are checked first; a peering is never left half made.
Private only, with -HubVnetId: link all of PIM Manager's own private zones (the Container Apps environment's, the database's and the registry's) to the hub. Your central zones are never touched.
external = the public install; internal = only with -PrivateNetwork, and a private install is always internal (the whole Container Apps environment has no public address).

parameters.usedWhen: the Pro copy of the launcher (trial / pro)
parameters.help: Pro: the update ring -- 2 = design partners, 3 = broad (the default).
Optional: the installation's own Key Vault name (the sign-in front's keys). Default kv-pim-<token>.
Who may sign in to the PIM Manager. Default: the super-admins.
Every member account of the tenant may sign in (guests never).

Optional. Also give the PIM engine User Access Administrator at the tenant root management group, so it can assign the Azure resource roles you delegate. Off by default: the engine always gets read-only Reader there (Discovery), and Get Started shows the command to add User Access Administrator later.
Default: you (the account running the install).

The mailbox PIM sends from. Created by the install when the installer holds an ACTIVE Exchange Administrator or Global Administrator role (both sending identities get the scoped send right); without one the install completes and the end-of-install check shows the Get Started > Mail sender command.

parameters.derivedFrom: -MailSender (without -MailSender the mail sender is left to your Exchange administrator; with -MailSender the install creates it)
parameters.help: On by default: the install creates no mailbox and gives the installing account no Exchange role; your own Exchange administrator sets up the mail sender afterwards (Get Started > Mail sender). Until then PIM Manager sends no mail. Naming a mailSender (with this off) lets the install create it.
Who gets the alerts (engine failures, drift, break-glass use, ...). Default: the super-admins' mailboxes. A list that is already set is never overwritten.
The Invardia Support app of this tenant (pre-filled from the support environment). Empty = no support access (the Support app is named by its id, never found by name).

troubleshoot = read the database and its schema; setup = also repair and upgrade (SQL admin group member, owner of PIM's own apps and groups); asbuilt = ONLY start the as-built job and read the PDF it writes (troubleshoot and setup include that too).

steps.title: Azure services in the chosen region
Sign-in front for the PIM Manager

requiredRights: Owner, or Contributor + User Access Administrator, on the subscription (required -- the preflight stops without it)
Privileged Role Administrator, active (recommended) -- without it the SQL admin group, the Graph permissions and the sign-in consent end as hand-off actions with the exact command
Exchange Administrator or Global Administrator, active, for the notification mailbox (optional -- without it the end-of-install check ends with the Get Started > Mail sender follow-up)

Owner or User Access Administrator at the tenant root management group (recommended; a Global Administrator who turned on Access management for Azure resources) -- the install gives the engine Reader there; without that right the end-of-install check ends with a WARNING and the exact command for that person (the install is not stopped -- owner decision of 2026-10-08)
runsIn: PowerShell 7 on the admin's own machine, signed in in the browser as your own administrator -- never a secret; no Azure CLI, no modules (PIM 2.4.554+)
licence: Never in the command. Community: none. Trial / Pro: added after the installation in PIM Manager > Settings > Licence -- a Pro licence bound to the tenant above (a trial or a paid licence); one for another tenant, or one that names no tenant, is refused there.
signIn: The PIM Manager signs people in through the sign-in front (no client secret): its state is kept in the PIM database, its keys are wrapped by the install's own Key Vault (Standard, RBAC, purge protection; -KeyVaultName, else kv-pim-<token>), and it passes an access token to the PIM Manager. -PortalUsers / -AllowAllMembers decide who may sign in.
costStatement: About 27 USD a month (Azure Container Apps scale to zero, Basic registry, Azure SQL Standard S0 -- the minimum, never Basic, 250 GB maximum size -- external; the sign-in front's Key Vault is Standard: no monthly fee, a few cents of key operations). A -PrivateNetwork install adds about 65 USD a month at list prices (the Premium registry about 50, two private endpoints about 7 each, plus their data processing), plus the registry's agent pool, billed by the hour while it exists (ACR Tasks prices).
